correctness.rationale: Explicit symmetric-matrix eigenvalues yield an implicit quadratic for F-b; its derivative has a single sign reversal precisely when b crosses 2/sqrt(alpha(alpha-4)). The exact F versus F(1) comparison localizes every positive overshoot to t=1-O(epsilon), b>=c/sqrt(epsilon). A differentiated square-root series is uniform in this full localized region even for b->infinity. Optimizing its limiting polynomial proves the coefficient 1/(100 sqrt 5) and all global maximizer scales. The checker passes finite tests; these are not substituted for the continuum proof.

value.rationale: A current primary theorem identifies 4 as the qualitative universal monotonicity exponent and supplies a single nonmonotone witness. The new result identifies the exact coefficient-dependent bifurcation, the unique moving maximizer, and the globally sharp five-halves amplitude and optimizer as the exponent crosses 4. This quantifies a structurally motivated failure of monotonicity in block-operator norms; the parameter optimization is not a routine substitution of the existing fifth-power example.
